findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cheese sauce to be hot holding at 110F. Discussed with PIC, cheese sauce was removed from warmer and reheated to 165F. Ensure any TCS item that is hot held is kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple TCS drink items without date marking. Items included grape and orange juice located at bar cooler. Discussed with PIC, items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly dated marked and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be stored on floor in walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, items were moved to shelving unit. Ensure any TCS item is stored at least 6 inches off of ground.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of debris on multiple nonfood contact surfaces:
(Repeat) 1) Rust on the shelves in the walk in cooler.

Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Shelves should be resealed or replaced by the next routine inspection. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, which may contaminate ready to eat (RTE) foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to have no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding the recommend concentration and process for testing. Sanitizer was observed at a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is made and tested at a frequency to verify the proper concentration for sanitizing food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed to go to cups of cheese sauce to be hot holding at 119F (verified via stem thermometer). CORRECTED- the 2 cups of cheese sauce were voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Discussed long term solutions with the PIC (either using time as control [foods are used or discarded within 4 hours and marked accordingly], OR filling the bulk container to ensure the warm water is transferring to multiple sides of the container, and then moving it into a to-go container at the time of service. Ensure any temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are hot held at or above 135F.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple sauces stored in 3 door reach in cooler to be held past 7 day max. Discussed with PIC, sauces were marked and discarded. Ensure staff is checking date marking on sauces to ensure sauces are not kept past maximum holding date. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

(REPEAT x2) Observed the shelving grates of the 3-door reach-in cooler and the walk-in cooler to be rusted and paint is chipping away. Shelving should be smooth, easily cleanable, and corrosion resistant (rusting is occurring). Shelving and/or grates need replaced or re-painted/re-sealed with clear coat. The bottom shelving of the prep tables in the center of the kitchen have rusted, as well. Shelving needs re-painted/re-sealed and/or appropriate plastic covering can be placed on the surface so it is easily cleanable (rusting, paint chipping away). Repeat violations since the last routine inspections on 3/15/23, 8/2/23, and 2/7/24. 

The ceiling vents in the kitchen have began to rust and paint is chipping away. The same issues are occurring. The ceiling vents need replaced and/or re-painted/re-sealed with clear coat. Repeat from 8/2/23 and 2/7/24 inspection

Discussed all repairs with PIC. Repair above areas by the next routine inspection.

dust on the grates.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT x2) Observed the following areas in need of repairs to make smooth, easily cleanable, non-absorbent, and durable:
1. The coving around the women’s bathroom is coming away from the wall. Many tiles have begun to fall and are propped up against the wall (not sealed and caulked). The men’s bathroom needs the coving caulked to the wall. Ensure both bathrooms have coving fixed by the next routine inspection.
2. The mop sink wall is no longer smooth and easily cleanable (water and wear damage). Mop basin needs caulked to the wall.
3. The 3 compartment sink (to the right of the dish machine) is missing caulking between the sink and wall. There are holes in the wall that need filled with caulk, as well. 

#1 is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/15/23, 8/2/23, and 2/7/24. 
#2 is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 8/2/23 and 2/7/24. 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed multiple food handling members of staff to not have food handlers licenses. Discussed with PIC, ensure all members of staff that handle food have food handlers licenses within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
